speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the onset of your double vision; did it start suddenly or gradually, and does the eye deviation change when you look toward the affected side? Also, has your difficulty climbing stairs or upper limb weakness been present since the same time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with double vision specifically on upward or downward gaze, strongly suggests a neuromuscular issue like Myasthenia Gravis. To confirm this, I need to see if your weakness is consistent across different muscle groups; have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty speaking clearly lately? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies, combined with fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and diplopia on vertical gaze, confirms this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. I will now request images of your ocular muscles and perform a specific bedside test to assess your respiratory muscle strength. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Thorax_and_Chest.
